titulo: Does turning the thermostat down at night save money?
fuentes: U.S. Department of Energy (Energy Saver): thermostats, turning back 7 to 10 degrees F for 8 hours a day can save as much as 10% a year on heating and cooling; generally not recommended for heat pumps

frases.texto: You leave the heat on all night because you think reheating the house costs more.

frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: A house loses heat faster when the gap between inside and outside is bigger.
So a cooler house leaks less heat, all night long.
The U.S. Department of Energy says turning your thermostat back seven to ten degrees for eight hours a day can save as much as ten percent a year.
Heads up: that's an upper estimate, and heat pumps are different, so check yours first.
Tonight, try dropping it a few degrees before bed.
Send this to the friend who set the thermostat to seventy-two and never touched it again.
